components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin

## Summary

Telephone is now stored and returned in E.164 form, with duplicate detection comparing E.164 values, and invalid numbers rejected with 400.

The E.164 conversion lives in one small, cohesive method so structural impact stays low — the two advice classes are tiny (low `WMC_other`), and I kept each edited method simple:

**`OwnerTelephoneNormalizationAdvice`** — replaced the "strip to exactly 10 digits" rule with a static `toE164(...)`:
- Keeps a leading `+` and its country code when present.
- Otherwise assumes `+61` and drops a single leading `0` from the national digits.
- Strips spaces/dashes/brackets (all non-digits), and requires 8–15 digits after the `+`, else throws → 400.
- e.g. `0412 345 678` → `+61412345678`, `+64 21 123 456` → `+6421123456`, `12` → rejected.

**`OwnerUniqueTelephoneAdvice`** — reuses `toE164(...)` and compares the resulting E.164 string directly against stored owners' E.164 telephones. It normalizes independently, so duplicate detection is correct regardless of advice ordering (matching the codebase's existing order-tolerant pattern; `toE164` is idempotent on already-E.164 values).

Two constraint relaxations were required so the `+`-prefixed value survives validation (both patterns previously demanded digits-only, which runs *after* normalization):
- **`Owner.java`** — swapped the `^[0-9]{10}$` `@Pattern` and `@Digits` for `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$` (JPA pre-persist validation).
- **`openapi.yml`** — updated the `telephone` pattern to `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$` (generated-DTO `@Valid` on the controller).
